meta.title: Morning at Green Hill
meta.textType: story: a morning routine told with pictures

paragraphs: Lily stayed at Grandma and Grandpa's house in Green Hill for the weekend. Pip came with her. Grandma got up at half past five every day. She fed the hens, watered the plants, and put bread in the oven. "I like the quiet morning," Grandma said. Grandpa got up at six o'clock. He watered the garden every morning.

On Sunday morning, Grandma was feeding the hens when Lily woke up at seven. Lily came out of the house and looked at the sky. Grandpa was watering the garden. "Good morning, lazy girl," he said with a smile. "I was tired," said Lily. Grandpa turned off the water. "We keep the village and the environment clean," he said. "Are you hungry?" asked Grandma. "Yes, very," said Lily. "Can I help you, Grandma?" she asked. "Yes, after breakfast," said Grandma. "Don't hurry."

During breakfast, Grandma cut the warm bread with a knife. Lily ate two big pieces. After breakfast, Grandpa cycled to the village shop for milk. Lily and Grandma left the house at nine o'clock. They went out of the gate and walked to the pond. Pip ran around the wood on the way. Pip was sniffing the grass when a frog jumped into the pond. "Hurry, Pip!" called Lily. Pip ran back to her.

They were home at eleven o'clock. Grandpa was waiting at the gate with the milk. Lily helped Grandma carry the plates to the kitchen. "Thank you, Lily," said Grandma. "Green Hill is a good place," said Lily. "Next weekend, I will get up at half past five, too!" Grandma laughed and smiled at her.
